smell: get_line_map bundles three distinct concerns — assembling named nodes, resolving each physical edge's disruption color by matching free-text route-section names against layout edges and picking the most-severe overlapping disruption, and delegating per-train position resolution — with the edge-color matching/ranking algorithm left inline rather than delegated, unlike the train-marker concern which the design already extracts into app.services.train_position_resolver / app.services.train_location_parser. This shows up as four distinct postcondition clauses on a single public method and six direct module dependencies (tfl_client, station_repository, line_layout_repository, models.line_layout, train_position_resolver, models.line_map).
improvement_instruction: Extract the route-section-to-physical-edge matching and most-severe-wins color resolution into its own module (e.g. app.services.line_edge_status_resolver) that takes a LineLayout's edges plus the line's RawLineStatus list and returns MapEdge entries with disruption_category set. Have line_map_service delegate to it the same way it already delegates train placement to train_position_resolver, leaving get_line_map as a thin orchestrator that fetches raw data and combines the two resolvers' outputs with the node list.
reason: When a bug is reported that a physical section shows the wrong disruption color (e.g. two overlapping disruptions on the same section resolve to the wrong severity), because the matching-and-ranking algorithm is inlined in the same function that also does data fetching and train-marker assembly, a developer cannot unit-test or reason about the edge-coloring rule in isolation the way train placement already can be tested via train_position_resolver — fixing or extending the color rule (e.g. adding a new severity category) requires exercising the entire get_line_map orchestration path instead of a small, independently testable resolver.
